title: DEC-57: review lore init's tracker-ready flow and land a draft ADR for the operator's stop-and-instruct approval (no implementation)
description: DEC-57 was decided 2026-09-29 by the operator (relayed by opum-agent; opum-doc relay ODOC-OP-2026-09-29-22): "Stop and instruct" — lore init must detect whether quest is both installed and quest-init-ed, stop with its own instructions when either is missing, never install or init any tracker (quest, jira or backlog), and retire the install offer. The operator requires a lore-cli review and a written workflow for their review and approval BEFORE any implementation (Article 5). This task carries the review and the write-up only: a draft ADR lands on dev (next free number, 0024, since 0023 is held on the parked branch chore/LCLI-653-bump-0.12.0) and its location plus a summary go to opum-agent for routing to opum-doc. Implementation is a separate task, created only after the operator approves the workflow. Why it matters now: opum-ai/lore-cli#433 (the 0.12.0 bump) is held as a draft because lint · typecheck · test (windows-latest), a required context, is red. Measured mechanism, 2026-09-29: test/cli.test.ts drives the real router through the wizard with no install seam (src/cli.ts forwards none), so on a runner without quest the install offer runs the real unpinned npm install -g @opum-ai/quest (npm latest = 0.11.0), later-loaded test files find it, and the lore 0.12.0 / quest 0.11.0 pair lock fails the LCLI-614 tests; ubuntu skips them. Retiring the offer removes the repository's only global-install site (src/adapters/tracker-environment.ts).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The current lore init tracker flow is reviewed and recorded state by state in the write-up: detection (installed + initialized per backend), the interactive offer, the non-interactive paths, jira/backlog/none behavior, and the measured Windows-vs-ubuntu CI mechanism with run ids

A draft ADR lands in docs/adr recording DEC-57 (the operator's answer and the option text verbatim), the proposed stop-and-instruct workflow with the exact message and exit code for every detected state, the --install-tracker/--no-install-tracker deprecation, and the effect on the Windows CI job and on opum-ai/lore-cli#433

The write-up location and a short summary are sent to opum-agent for routing to opum-doc, and no behavior change is implemented in this delivery: nothing under src/ or test/ is modified (Article 5, awaiting operator approval)

implementationNotes: 2026-09-29: ADR-0024 REVISED on this branch per the operator's refinement, relayed by opum-agent and read from its provenance (opum-doc seq 45, ODOC-OP-2026-09-29-26, 2026-09-29T21:41:40Z). The operator did NOT approve the first draft; the offers return: quest-not-installed and quest-not-initialized each offer a stop whose YES prints exact install/init commands and exits (lore runs nothing), whose NO returns to the tracker question; a detected backlog.md project offers stop-and-migrate with the exact commands; the JIRA offer is NOT included because no runnable JIRA->Quest migration exists (measured: quest 0.11.0 exposes only `migration backlog`; quest-cli dev carries a qualified importer — QCLI-74/QCLI-89 Done — with no CLI command). The revision answers all seven of opum-doc's questions: the two state x answer validation tables (O1-O12 interactive, N1-N10 non-interactive), precedence (offers fire on selection, quest then backlog then jira; a no never auto-skips the rest), no-TTY (stop with the instructions, never continue-as-no), exit codes (3/6 still fit: the class names the state, not the consent), Backlog commands named exactly (`lore init --tracker quest --migrate-backlog`, `quest migration backlog preview|apply`, with the LORE_QUEST_ACTOR actor context), and points 4/5 restated (tightened explicit --tracker; bare-init and --no-tracker unchanged). Nothing under src/ or test/ changed; frontmatter stays status: draft; branch realigned with origin/dev (merge; docs/log.md handoff lines; lore sync regenerated the ADR index title). Next: head SHA + the tables go to opum-agent for the operator's approval; #436 stays held and unlanded.
